case.pattern_description: Threshold structuring on a compromised card: 4 online purchases ($457.09, $492.56, $455.25, $479.86) placed within about an hour, each kept just under $500, the level at which authorisation checks tighten. It affects cardholders whose card numbers are already compromised and matches five closed cases the bank confirmed but could not map to a known typology; the agent found it by scanning the card's window for clusters of same-band amounts.

sar.narrative: Customer C05423, holder of card C05423-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-12-03 12:00 and 2016-12-03 12:30, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,884.76 were made on the card online from device profile 'Windows |  | chrome 65.0 | ': $457.09 (3509526, 2016-12-03 12:00), $492.56 (3509535, 2016-12-03 12:06), $455.25 (3509563, 2016-12-03 12:22), $479.86 (3509576, 2016-12-03 12:30). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: Case-memory model score 0.492; 4 online purchases within 30 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($457.09, $492.56, $455.25, $479.86; total $1,884.76). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3841, CC-4124, CC-3907. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placed linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
